key_insight: Layerwise token dynamics in realistic finite-depth, finite-width transformers with MLP blocks converge pathwise to a continuous-time stochastic interacting particle system; the tokens' distribution satisfies a derived SPDE and noise can induce synchronization, with propagation of chaos holding as token count grows.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between discrete layerwise transformer dynamics and continuum stochastic descriptions for finite models, providing quantitative, commuting limits and rigorous control of how noise shapes collective token behaviour.
method: Prove pathwise convergence of the discrete layerwise evolution to a continuous-time stochastic interacting particle system for finite depth and width.
Derive the governing stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) for the tokens' distribution and prove propagation of chaos as the number of tokens → ∞.
Establish quantitative bounds and show the different scaling/limiting operations commute (finite-to-continuum and many-tokens limits).
impact: Gives practitioners a principled stochastic continuum framework to analyze and predict transformer dynamics in realistic finite settings, clarifying how injected or intrinsic noise can synchronize activations and affect training/robustness.
visual_elements: Schematic: discrete transformer layers (tokens flowing through attention + MLP) morphing into a continuous-time interacting particle system.
Diagram: convergence/limits map showing discrete model → particle system → SPDE and commuting arrows for finite/large-token limits.
Heatmap/animation: evolution of token density over continuous time from the SPDE (shows diffusion, clustering, synchronization).
Trajectory plot: multiple token paths under noise illustrating synchronization by noise (paths aligning over layers/time).
paper_title: Stochastic Scaling Limits and Synchronization by Noise in Deep Transformer Models
paper_authors: Andrea Agazzi, Giuseppe Bruno, Eloy Mosig García, Samuele Saviozzi, Marco Romito
